brief.topic: Myth: a bigger model will fix our hallucinations
brief.audience: PMs and engineers shipping RAG and chat features
constraints: Example cases labelled illustrative on screen and in caption

coreInsight: Many product hallucinations come from missing or stale sources, prompts that never allow “I don’t know”, or missing tools — a bigger model can’t supply facts it never saw, so check inputs first.

caption.opening: “Let’s just use a bigger model” is the most expensive way to not fix a hallucination.
body:
Typical causes that look like model errors:
→ Stale data: the index was never refreshed
→ Retrieval: the right document never reached the prompt
→ Missing tool: no way to check live facts like order status
→ Prompt: nothing allows “I don’t know”
Check those in order, cheapest first. Then, if answers are still wrong, test a bigger model on your own eval set and compare.
(The cases in the reel are illustrative examples, not measured data.)

claims.text: Many hallucinations in products come from retrieval gaps, stale data, missing tools or prompts that forbid uncertainty; a larger model cannot supply facts it never received.
Four example symptoms and their causes.
